descriptionChirho: The base metal tin, listed alongside other metals in prophetic and trade contexts (Ezek 22:18, 22:20, 27:12; Num 31:22). Multilingual evidence consistently renders this as a specific metal: (eng: tin / and-tin, spa: estaño / y-estaño, arb: وَقَصِديرٍ / وَقَصِديرٌ, hin: टिन / और-टिन, kor: 주석 / 그리고-주석, swa: bati / na-bati). Arabic قَصِدير and Spanish estaño are the standard words for tin, confirming this as the literal metallurgical sense of the word.

A plumb-line or plummet instrument, so called because it was weighted with tin or lead, used metaphorically for divine judgment and measurement (Amos 7:7-8). The translations diverge sharply from the bare-metal sense: (eng: the-plumb, spa: la-de-plomo, hin: टिन-के, arb: الْمُعَلَّقَةِ, kor: 그-다림추의, swa: la-risasi). Spanish plomo (lead), Korean 다림추 (plumb-bob), and Swahili risasi (lead/bullet) all point to a weighted measuring device rather than raw tin as a commodity.

Tin or base-metal impurity mixed into silver, used figuratively for moral corruption and spiritual unfaithfulness (Isa 1:25). The multilingual signatures clearly separate this from both the raw metal and the plumb-line senses: (eng: your-alloy, spa: tu-impureza, hin: तेरी-मिलावट, arb: قَصدِيرِكِ, kor: 네-불순물, swa: uchafu-wako). Spanish impureza (impurity), Hindi मिलावट (adulteration), Korean 불순물 (impurity), and Swahili uchafu (filth/impurity) all converge on the concept of contaminating dross rather than tin as a standalone substance.
